text:
alex.k: Heads up — multiple EU customers reporting 2000ms+ tail latency and intermittent 401s this morning. They say requests are being routed to us-west instead of eu-west.
alex.k: Repro steps from customer:
alex.k: curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
alex.k: sometimes 200 OK, sometimes 401 + long delay. tcpdump on their side shows SYN->SYN/ACK fast, but app-level latency is high.
maya.ops: I see a spike in gateway errors at 09:12 UTC, lots of upstream resets. logs:
maya.ops: [09:12:18] gateway edge-proxy router: upstream_reset: reset reason: connection failure; upstream_host: gw-us-west-2-03
sam.chen: do we have a header rewrite rule that might be dropping X-Region-Hint on certain routes? last change to steering config was commit b2f4c1 (traffic steering v2.3.4)
devon.eng: yep — v2.3.4 introduced a small L7 hostrewrite for legacy tenants. The rewrite flow strips all x-* headers for safety then re-injects a allowlist. x-region-hint wasn't on the allowlist.
priya.support: That would explain customers seeing US endpoints and auth tokens invalidating (tokens bound to region presence for our auth layer). :grimacing:
alex.k: Can we reproduce internally? I ran:
alex.k: curl -H 'X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid-eu-token>' https://edge.internal.redwood/gateway/route -v
alex.k: Response headers show: \nHTTP/1.1 200 OK\nX-Proxy-Routed-To: us-west-2\nX-Auth-Status: token-bound-to-eu (was expected)\nBut then auth check returns 401 downstream since token metadata missing.
maya.ops: Repro: I toggled the hostrewrite rule off on one node and requests preserved X-Region-Hint consistently and routed to eu pool.
infra-bot: incident.alert: 3 customers impacted; avg extra latency 1.8s; rollback candidate: revert hostrewrite allowlist change.
devon.eng: Quick mitigation: add x-region-hint to allowlist and redeploy router config (no restart). Patch: add header_preserve: ["x-region-hint","x-forwarded-host","x-api-version"].
sam.chen: Note: we should also ensure auth service treats absence of X-Region-Hint as unknown and not auto-fallback to token validation path that invalidates. That fallback is causing billing/usage discrepancies because requests are routed to different capacity class.
priya.support: I'll notify the affected customers with workaround (append ?region=eu-west to queries) and that we're rolling config change now.
devon.eng: Rolling change pushed to edge config cluster in EU and global control plane. Watchers on prometheus: gateway.route.miss and auth.401.
maya.ops: After config push, counters show x-region header preserved, routing stabilized to eu pool, 401 rate down to baseline in last 3 mins. latency back to normal for sampled traces.
alex.k: Thanks team. Follow-up: create a retro issue to add a unit test in routing for header-preservation so future hostrewrite changes don't regress this. Also check billing metering for the affected window.
priya.support: Logged SUPPORT-5698 with customer notes and repro steps + timeline.
infra-bot: incident.resolve: mitigation applied; monitoring for 30m; assigned to devon.eng for postmortem.
